chainlinkOracleNote: C-6 launch resolution: the protocol now uses Chainlink Data Feeds DIRECTLY (the `chainlinkOracle` block below), not the bespoke median. That block is populated with on-chain-verified Base addresses (WETH via ETH/USD, cbBTC via BTC/USD, the Base L2 sequencer feed, USDC pinned) and passes `scripts/verify-chainlink-oracle.mjs` (12/12). Deploy path: DeployChainlinkOracle.s.sol -> verify -> BLESSED_ORACLES -> Deploy.s.sol. The `blockingNote` below applies ONLY to the deferred custom-aggregator sections, which the C-6 factory allowlist makes non-selectable at launch anyway.
blockingNote: (DEFERRED custom-oracle path only — superseded by chainlinkOracle for launch.) THIS SECTION CANNOT BE DEPLOYED AS WRITTEN. Three independent constructor requirements added by the security remediation now reject it, and each needs a human decision plus real on-chain addresses that must not be invented: (1) H-1 — every asset carries quorum 2, and OracleAggregator now requires quorum >= MIN_MEDIAN (3), because a two-element lower median is a MINIMUM, not a median; (2) H-1 again — with only 3 sources per asset, quorum 3 means any single dark source freezes the asset, so each asset needs >= 5 sources to have BOTH median integrity and failure headroom, i.e. two further independently-operated sources per asset whose addresses are not in this file; (3) H-2 — twapDefaults pairs windowSeconds 1800 with maxObservationAgeSeconds 3600, and UniswapV3TwapSource now requires maxObservationAge <= window / 20 (= 90s at this window), because the newest observation age is exactly the live tick's weight in the reported mean. Both rejections are pinned as tests: MixedOracleSources::test_remediated_theOldThreeSourceQuorumTwoShapeIsRejected and AuditTwapRealCostModel::test_remediated_constructorRejectsMaxObsAgeAboveTheWindowFraction. The on-chain verification below remains TRUE of the addresses it checked, and is retained for that reason — but it is now evidence about a configuration that no longer builds. Re-run scripts/verify-mainnet-config.mjs after rebuilding, and note M-12: that script cannot observe maxObservationAgeSeconds at all, so it would not have caught (3).
rebuildChecklist: Choose 2 further sources per asset (mechanism- or at least operator-diverse; see MixedOracleSources.t.sol for why operator diversity has to carry the 4th and 5th slots while only three mechanism classes are implemented), and record their real Base mainnet addresses.

Set quorum to 3 for every asset (MIN_MEDIAN, strict majority of 5, and two failures of headroom). ⚠ C-6: quorum 3 of 5 is only a FAULT-TOLERANCE floor — it tolerates exactly ONE adversarial source (a=1). It is NOT Byzantine-safe against two: a single honest leg withholding drops the fresh set to 4 and two controlled sources own the lower median (re-opening C-4's 88.9% theft). Byzantine safety needs quorum >= 2a+1 and m >= 2a+f+1. m=5 CANNOT tolerate a=2 with any fault tolerance. So EITHER guarantee the 5 sources are genuinely independent with no single actor controlling >1 (a listing/curation requirement the contract cannot enforce), OR list m>=7 for a=2, OR — recommended — abandon the custom aggregator and consume Chainlink Data Feeds directly (already Byzantine-tolerant at the node-operator layer). See AI-AUDIT-REPORT.md C-6.

Set twapDefaults.maxObservationAgeSeconds <= windowSeconds / 20. At window 1800 that is 90. A pool too quiet to satisfy 90s needs a LONGER window, not a looser age — the ratio is the contamination bound.
Re-check every pool's observationCardinality against the (possibly longer) window before deploying.
Re-run scripts/verify-mainnet-config.mjs, and treat its 22/22 as necessary rather than sufficient (M-12).

H-8: set every vault's minDepositUsdc to an economically meaningful value relative to its capacity (the smoke template now uses 100 USDC). The <5-member signer quorum regime is stake-blind, so a cheap minimum deposit lets an attacker buy the regime flip or grief a small vault into ungovernability. There is no safe contract floor (M-6 shape); this is a listing constraint.

usdcNote: Circle-native USDC on Base (6 decimals). NOT USDbC (0xd9aA...4CA2), the bridged legacy token. Getting this wrong silently prices every vault against the wrong dollar.
maxStalenessNote: One hour, NOT the 'tight (minutes)' figure DEPLOYMENT.md §2 recommends for a pure push-feed stack. That advice is correct for Chainlink and wrong for a stack containing a pull oracle: the Pyth leg only advances when a keeper pays to post, so a 60-second bound drops it from the fresh set on most reads and silently demotes 2-of-3 into 2-of-2 with no failure headroom (asserted in test/MixedOracleSources.t.sol::test_tightStalenessSilentlyDemotesPullLegAndRemovesHeadroom). Tighten this only after measuring the observed worst-case on-chain publish gap for the pinned price ids, or after funding a keeper at a known cadence. Ceiling is 1 day (OracleAggregator.MAX_STALENESS_CEILING).
pythNote: Pyth receiver contract. UNVERIFIED. Pyth deploys the same address across many chains, which makes a copy-paste error from another chain's docs indistinguishable from a correct entry — verify `code.length > 0` on Base specifically, and that getPriceUnsafe returns for each id below.
pythMaxConfBpsNote: Reject a Pyth reading whose confidence interval exceeds 1% of price — a feed in disagreement with itself declines to vote rather than casting an uncertain one. Ceiling is 2000 (PythSource.MAX_CONF_BPS_CEILING).

twapDefaults.maxObservationAgeBlockingNote: REJECTED BY THE CURRENT CONTRACTS (H-2). 3600 against a 1800s window meant the newest observation could be TWICE the window old while guard 3 still passed — and the newest-observation age IS the live tick's weight in the reported mean (min(A,W)/W), so this permitted a reported '30-minute TWAP' composed entirely of a single live tick, stamped zero seconds old. The constructor now requires maxObservationAge <= window / 20; at window 1800 the loosest legal value is 90.
twapDefaults.minCardinalityNote_L4: L-4 FIXED: this was 900, which is off by one. A ring of C slots spans (C-1) x blocktime, so 900 slots cover 1798s against an 1800s window and the constructor reverts; 901 succeeds. It failed closed and was never triggered by the live pools (5000/2000/5000), but it would have bitten the next asset listing. If the window lengthens during the #41 rebuild, recompute: minCardinality = windowSeconds/blocktime + 1.
twapDefaults.cardinalityNote: A V3 pool writes at most ONE observation per block, only on a swap. Base targets 2-second blocks, so covering a 1800-second window in the worst case (a swap every block) needs 1800/2 = 900 slots. `increaseObservationCardinalityNext` is permissionless but the growth is paid per slot (roughly 20k gas each; ~18M gas to go from 1 to 900, so it is done incrementally over several transactions). Check each pool's current `observationCardinality` via slot0() BEFORE deploying: UniswapV3TwapSource's constructor rejects a pool that cannot already serve the window, which is the intended failure — grow the cardinality first, then deploy.
twapDefaults.windowNote: 30 minutes. Bounds are [300, 86400] (MIN_WINDOW/MAX_WINDOW). Longer resists manipulation better and tracks a moving market worse; this is the SF-1 knob, and it is immutable per source.

assets.quorumNote: REJECTED BY THE CURRENT CONTRACTS (H-1). This note used to read: '2 of 3 — the strict-majority floor, and the only value that both satisfies the constructor and leaves one source of failure headroom.' Both halves were true and the conclusion was still wrong: at two FRESH sources the aggregator returns fresh[0], the minimum, not a median — a one-directional downward price selector, and downward is the direction that mints excess shares (C-4). The headroom concern was real; the answer is 5 sources with quorum 3, not quorum 2 with 3. Left at 2 deliberately so this file fails loudly at construction rather than looking deployable.

smoke.minDepositNote: H-8 (2026-08-28): raised from 1 USDC to 100 USDC. The `<5`-member signer quorum regime is stake-blind — it counts any address with shares > 0 — so it is only Sybil-resistant when acquiring the ~4 seats needed to flip the regime (H-8(a)) or to grief a small vault into ungovernability costs a materially non-trivial sum. `minDepositUsdc` is the per-seat cost. There is NO safe contract-level floor for this (a fraction-of-stake floor repeats M-6's liveness cliff; an absolute floor equal to the deposit minimum is what an attacker already pays), so it is a documented LISTING constraint: set minDepositUsdc high enough, relative to capacity, that manufacturing dust members is expensive. See AI-AUDIT-REPORT.md H-8 and THREAT-MODEL.md CM-7.
smoke.govDefencesNote: M-6: these three were 0 / 10000 / 0 — i.e. the reference configuration shipped with every named CM-6/VO-5 defence DISABLED. proposalThresholdBps 0 let anyone holding one unit open proposals (the precondition M-7 and C-1 both rely on); concentrationCapBps 10000 let a single delegate carry 100% of snapshot stake, so one live participant plus a permissionless cranker manufactured full quorum from offline delegators, defeating VO-2 outright; proposalCooldown was not validated by the contract AT ALL. Governance._validateConfig now enforces a 100 bps threshold floor, a 5000 bps concentration ceiling, and a proposalCooldown in [1 hour, 30 days] — the upper bound because an unvalidated uint32 cooldown is C-2's shape on a field C-2 did not cover.
smoke.govChosenValuesNote: Chosen deliberately above the contract floors rather than at them: 500 bps (5%) to propose is a real stake requirement without excluding a genuine minority holder; 4000 bps caps a delegate at 40% of received weight, leaving quorum dependent on more than one participant; 21600 s (6 h) of cooldown is well clear of the 1 h floor and rate-limits the propose-defeat-propose cycle that holds exits in Mode F (M-7). A launch config should not sit on a security floor - the floor is what stops a hostile creator, not what a careful one picks.
smoke.govNote: Unlike base-sepolia.json this sets a non-zero timelockDuration: a testnet smoke run wants zero delay, mainnet capital wants a day to react to a passed proposal.
